entry.title: Listen to Olivia Rodrigo’s New Song “Take Me Home (4 Christmas)”
entry.summary: "I'm so thoughtful and merry and kind, and I was waiting a really long time"
entry.content:
All Olivia Rodrigo wants for Christmas is for her partner’s grandma to think she’s cool. Rodrigo just shared her first holiday song, aptly titled “Take Me Home (4 Christmas),” and it’s all about that first time you meet your honey’s extended family on their turf. Written with usual suspects Dan Nigro and Amy Allen, it’s accompanied by a music video starring Saturday Night Live’s Ben Marshall as Rodrigo’s boo, and Cynthia Nixon as his mom. Watch it below.

“Take Me Home” is Rodrigo’s follow-up to the David Byrne-starring video for her “Expectations” remix with tourmate Chappell Roan. Both songs featured on her 2026 album You Seem Pretty Sad For a Girl So in Love, which she’s currently bringing around the world on the Unraveled Tour. Her opening lineup features Grace Ives, Wolf Alice, Devon Again, the Last Dinner Party, and Die Spitz.

Earlier this year, Rodrigo also launched her own benefit music festival, Daisy Chain Fields. The inaugural edition, which took place in California in August and was inspired by Lilith Fair, gathered an age-diverse lineup of female artists from Quiet Light to the Breeders. At the even, which raised $20 million for sponsors like Planned Parenthood and Center for Reproductive Rights, Rodrigo also debuted a new song inspired by The Handmaids Tale, “Serena Joy.”

entry.title: Toro y Moi Reveals New Album Unusua
entry.summary: The project, which quietly appeared on Chaz Bear’s Bandcamp page, drops this month
entry.content:
In October, Toro y Moi premiered the supposedly one-off, piano-driven single “Proof.” Turns out it’s part of a new self-produced album called Unusua. Not much is known about the seven-track LP, which quietly appeared on Chaz Bear’s Bandcamp page in recent days, but Pitchfork has confirmed it’s out November 20. You can listen to “Proof” below.

Earlier this year, Toro y Moi released an acoustic version of his 2025 album Hole Erth and opened for Haruomi Hosono on the latter’s Stateside dates.

Revisit Larry Fitzmaurice’s 2013 interview with Toro y Moi.

entry.title: GloRilla and Sexyy Red Wreak Havoc on a Nursing Home in “Jiggly Bow Bow” Video
entry.summary: The two rappers have teamed up again for a high-energy single
entry.content:
While GloRilla puts the final touches on her second album, she has invited Sexyy Red on what looks like a preview of the new project, the crunk-inspired “Jiggly Bow Bow.” Scroll down to watch the music video, which sees the rappers as elderly versions of themselves throwing a full-blown rager at a nursing home.

GloRilla and Sexyy Red first collaborated on “Whatchu Kno About Me,” a single off GloRilla’s 2024 debut album, Glorious. They have since worked together on other musicians’ songs, like Tyler, the Creator’s “Sticky,” which also included Lil Wayne, and Summer Walker’s “Baller,” where they featured alongside Monaleo.

Read Pitchfork’s review of GloRilla’s Anyways, Life’s Great… EP.

entry.title: Lady Gaga, Jack White, Blondie Lead 2027 Songwriters Hall of Fame Nominees
entry.summary: Additional finalists include P!nk, Shakira, and ZZ Top
entry.content:
Lady Gaga, Jack White, Blondie’s Debbie Harry and Chris Stein, and other artists have been nominated for the Songwriters Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027. As is tradition, the nominees are divided into two categories for performing and non-performing songwriters, with three artists selected from each to be inducted. Voting concludes on December 14, with the final honorees being announced early next year.

Shakira, P!nk, Sia, and ZZ Top’s Dusty Hill, Billy Gibbons, and the late Frank Beard are also part of the performing songwriters group. Rounding out that batch of nominees are America’s Gerry Beckley and Dewey Bunnell, Boy George, Ne-Yo, Vince Gill, Grandmaster Melle Mel, and members of War.

Meanwhile, the non-performing songwriters category features Kandi Burruss, who wrote TLC’s “No Scrubs” and Destiny’s Child’s “Bills, Bills, Bills”; Pete Bellotte, who penned Donna Summer’s “Hot Stuff” and “I Feel Love”; Stargate, the production duo behind Beyoncé’s “Irreplaceable” and Rihanna’s “Diamonds”; Boy Meets Girl, who wrote Whitney Houston’s “I Wanna Dance With Somebody” and “How Will I Know”; Dan Wilson, whose enduring hits include Semisonic’s “Closing Time” and Adele’s “Someone Like You”; Andreas Carlsson, who co-wrote Backstreet Boys’ “I Want It That Way” and *NSYNC’s “Bye Bye Bye”; and Stock Aitken Waterman, who the internet can thank for Rick Astley’s “Never Gonna Give You Up.”

At the start of 2026, the Songwriters Hall of Fame inducted Taylor Swift (who was inexplicably introduced by Steven Spielberg), Alanis Morissette, Kenny Logins, KISS’s Gene Simmons and Paul Stanley, Tricky Stewart, and more.

entry.title: Tim Reaper Announces Debut Album World’s End
entry.summary: Hyperdub is releasing the record in February
entry.content:
After releasing a couple of self-released projects in 2025, the UK-based jungle producer Tim Reaper is dropping his debut solo album, World’s End, next year. Hyperdub will premiere the project on February 19, and today Reaper has shared the first single, the marching band-inspired “Roll Call.”

World’s End builds on Reaper’s jungle foundation while taking inspiration from gqom, footwork, drill, and techno. In a press statement, Reaper explained he was inspired to toy with other genres following the release of his 2024 EP, Scorched Earth. “Scorched Earth EP was inspired by a conversation I had with a mate where he was asking how I define ‘jungle’—and for me, jungle is mainly about the breakbeats and the tempo, but it could have anything else going on within that template,” he said. “The realisation made me want to challenge myself to try and bring in newer, lesser referenced sounds.”

entry.title: NewJeans’ Contracts Removed Key Protections Against Child Labor Violations
entry.summary: The beleaguered K-pop group’s dispute with HYBE label ADOR is laid bare in a New York Times report
entry.content:
Last year, NewJeans staged a revolt over strict contracts that challenged the foundations of the K-pop industry. Their case, against the HYBE label ADOR, hinged on the claim they had suffered “significant negligence” at the hands of their employers. ADOR beat them in court and proceeded to fire Danielle Marsh from the band; her lawyer said the label was punishing her for the attempted mutiny. Now, ADOR is pursuing millions in damages from Marsh for breach of contract. But questions remain over the severity of the conditions to which ADOR subjected NewJeans—a battery of brutal training regimes and unusually strict personal terms that are laid out in a new report from The New York Times.

The harsh reality of K-pop contracts is no secret. So notoriously gruelling are the demands on trainee idols that the Korean government has a contract template to forestall the most inhumane conditions. But labels are free to stray from its recommendations, and ADOR made several key changes, multiple experts told The Times. Standard language from the template—guaranteeing rights to education, physical and mental health, and other protections against child labor—was omitted from NewJeans’ contract, signed when the members were aged 14 to 17. Their parents accepted the terms. But when the mother of one member requested changes, ADOR’s vice president responded, in an email obtained by The Times, “If you do not agree to the current contract draft, including the points above, it may be best to reconsider the contract itself.”

In the lead-up to the band’s debut in 2022, ADOR drilled the young NewJeans members with little respite, the report suggests. Four of the five members dropped out of school. They often rehearsed late into the night, sometimes until 2 a.m., and breaks were discouraged, sources told The Times. (HYBE said it fully complies with child-protection laws, works hard to ensure performers’ safety, and does not pressure them to quit school or penalize them for resting.) The contracts gave the label the right to use A.I.-generated NewJeans voices indefinitely, whereas the government contract template returns rights to a performer for their name, image, and voice once the contract ends.

Other unusual restrictions in the contracts included bans on “insincere attitude,” “inappropriate romantic relationships,” and publicly stating “true or false facts” that could damage the label. Band member Hanni Pham nonetheless denounced ADOR for its treatment of her and her bandmates in a 2024 testimony to the Korean Parliament. Soon after, the band rebranded as NJZ and performed at ComplexCon in Hong Kong, in defiance of an injunction that a Seoul court granted to ADOR. But the rebellion was swiftly shut down as NewJeans—or NJZ—announced a hiatus in respect of the court order.

The strict contract terms meant insubordinate members could face massive lawsuits and fees. In terminating Marsh’s contract and suing her, ADOR alleged that her refusal to work—as well as unauthorized solo projects and photo shoots—broke the contract terms and cost the label some $22 million. The other NewJeans members remain under contract until 2029. Their latest activity is a video that ADOR posted last August, promising a “summer of NewJeans” that did not come to pass.

Are NewJeans Really Back?

entry.title: Rush Announce Sphere Residency
entry.summary: The five-date Elevate From the Norm set kicks off in May
entry.content:
Prog legends Rush are in the midst of their nearly yearlong Fifty Something reunion tour, which was originally set to wrap next spring. The band—co-founders Geddy Lee and Alex Lifeson, alongside drummer Anika Nilles and keyboardist Loren Gold—will play five nights at the globular Las Vegas venue in May. entry.title: Muna Tap Avalon Emerson, Romy for Dancing on the Wall Deluxe
entry.summary: The deluxe includes “Dancing on the Wall (Romy in a Lesbian Trance Remix)”
entry.content:
Thankfully safe and sound after an October tour bus fire, Muna are bouncing back with a deluxe edition of their May album Dancing on the Wall. The new extended cut features reworks from Avalon Emerson, Arlo Parks, and Porches, plus a “Dancing On The Wall (Romy in a Lesbian Trance Remix).” You’ll have to wait to hear that last one, but you can check out “Dancing on the Wall (Avalon Emerson Sweet Thing Remix)” now.

“We really revere Avalon as a DJ and we were so excited that she was down to do something for this song,” Muna shared in press materials. Emerson added: “Sometimes the remix fairy visits at just the right time, bearing gifts. When I heard ‘Dancing On The Wall,’ I thought it was really catchy, had a lot of color to paint with, and the pace and energy were in the realm where I could make something for the dance floor.” The full deluxe arrives on November 13 via Dead Oceans.

entry.title: Geese and Sunflower Bean Members Unite on New Album
entry.summary: The latest from side project Star’s Revenge lands at the end of the month
entry.content:
Star’s Revenge, the New York-based side project of Sunflower Bean’s Olive Faber and Geese guitarist Emily Green, have a new album due. Star’s Revenge II arrives on November 27, and you can listen to the lead single, “Don’t Worry Dynamite,” below.

The new project, which follows Faber and Green’s 2024 debut LP as Star’s Revenge, will match the duo with more heads from the New York scene: Turnip King drummer Christian Billard and the bassist Jonny Ceballos, whose bands include Outremont and the Paranoyds. Star’s Revenge II was recorded live at Billard’s home studio in Long Island.

Correction: A previous version of this story said Olive Faber was a guitarist in Sunflower Bean; she’s the band’s drummer but handles guitar and vocals in Star’s Revenge.

entry.title: Pink Floyd Reissuing Animals for 50th Anniversary
entry.summary: Animals 50 includes the unreleased Roger Waters song “Young Nicholas Jon,” plus unearthed versions of “Sheep” and “Dogs”
entry.content:
Pink Floyd are celebrating the 50th anniversary of their classic album Animals with an expansive new reissue. Animals 50, which lands via Sony on January 22, contains multiple unheard tracks—including the Roger Waters solo cut “Young Nicholas Jon” and unreleased versions of “Sheep” and “Dogs.” Listen to “Sheep (Original Radio Edit)” below.

Animals 50 will be available in multiple formats, including CD, vinyl, and download. The original tracklist is augmented by a full recording of the band’s 1977 show at Oakland Coliseum Arena, filmed by teen bootlegger Reinhard Hohlwein. The box set comes with a 64-page book with liner notes from author Jonathan Lethem, an interview with Hohlwein, and an excerpt from the memoir of Hipgnosis’ Aubrey “Po” Powell about the creation of Animals’ cover art. The book also includes a number of unpublished images, including photos from the album recording, the cover shoot at Battersea Power Station, and the tour behind the release.

David Gilmour said in press materials, “The mood in music was changing in ’77. Punk music was hitting everything and I suspect that had a little bit of an influence on the way we were working on the Animals album. I mean it’s quite an aggressive, stripped-back album. It was moving away from the sort of soundscapes that we had on Wish You Were Here. This album is more in your face and more rough and ready.”

Last year, Pink Floyd shared a 50th anniversary reissue of the aforementioned Wish You Were Here.

entry.title: Watch This Is Lorelei Play The Singer in My Band Songs on KCRW
entry.summary: Nate Amos brought five tracks from his latest album to the public radio station
entry.content:
This is Lorelei dropped by the Santa Monica public radio station KCRW today to perform five songs from his latest album The Singer in My Band. Accompanied by a four-piece band of bassist Al Nardo, keyboardist Bailey Wollowitz, and drummer Cameron Wisch, he played “I Will Eat My Heart In The Morning Light,” “Billy Came Back,” “Watching Heaven Fall,” and the title track. He closed things out with “The Kid With The Crown.” Check out the set below.

The Singer in My Band came out in September, and marked Amos’ first record for his new label, Matador. He’s supporting the album, which he has called a “road record,” on the road right now, accompanied by a roster of openers including Bleachers and @. A true ramblin’ man, he spent this past summer touring with his other band, Water From Your Eyes, who shared their most recent album, It’s a Beautiful Place, in 2025.

Revisit Marissa Lorusso’s review of This is Lorelei’s 2024 debut Box for Buddy, Box for Star.

entry.title: Bob Dylan, Wearing Hoodie, Meets Pope
entry.summary: Not quite Heaven’s door, but close
entry.content:
Pope Leo XIV granted Bob Dylan a private audience at the Vatican this morning (November 4), further cementing his downtown bona fides after welcoming Patti Smith in July. Dylan, the mythically private and fuss-refusing Nobel laureate, wore a black hoodie, hood up—seemingly held aloft by a black baseball cap—for the occasion, in evidence in a photo published by the Vatican’s Dicastery for Communication. Another photo seemingly shows Dylan signing a book for His Holiness, having removed a single glove.

Although raised Jewish, Dylan converted to evangelical Christianity in 1978. He released a string of Christian albums and peppered his live show with Christian songs—astounding legions of fans and contemporaries—but dialed down the religious fervor in subsequent years, primarily expressing his accord with God through the medium of ludicrous Christmas songs. In 1997, he played at a concert honoring Pope John Paul II.

Pope Leo, for his part, appears to be quite the Dylan scholar. He quoted the little-known Dylan lyric “Go Away You Bomb”—written in 1963 for an unpublished book of anti-nuclear poetry—in the preface to Unarmed and Disarming: Peace Is a Gift, an anthology of his speeches.

entry.title: Four Tet Produced a Tech-House Remix for the Durutti Column
entry.summary: “When I was asked to do a remix it felt like the universe was confirming I was connected to this music”
entry.content:
Before this year, the Manchester band the Durutti Column hadn’t released an album since 2010, but that hasn’t stopped its fanbase from growing. Vini Reilly’s project has inspired Harry Styles, Blood Orange, the Avalanches, and now, Four Tet—who created a hazy tech-house rework of “Your Shadow at Morning” from the Durutti Column’s 2026 album, Renascent.

“It’s only in the last couple of years that I learnt about the Durutti Column and explored their wonderful catalogue,” says Four Tet. “It’s had a big impact on me so I was thrilled when a new album was announced and then when I was asked to do a remix it felt like the universe was confirming I was connected to this music.”

Revisit Pitchfork’s review of The Return of the Durutti Column (Expanded & Remastered).

entry.title: Christine and the Queens Returns with Two New Songs
entry.summary: “Rendez-vous avec toi” arrives alongside an English counterpart, “Rendez-vous in your arms”
entry.content:
It’s been three years since Christine and the Queens shared his last proper solo album, a 20-song record inspired by Angels in America. Now, he’s back with a new song done up two ways: in French (“Rendez-vous avec toi”) and English (“Rendez-vous in your arms”). They both come with a music video co-directed by Chris and Raphaël De Albuquerque, with choreography by Alexander Ekman. Check out both versions below.

“Rendez-vous avec toi” and “Rendez-vous in your arms” are the first preview of a still-untitled new album from Christine and the Queens, which is due out sometime this spring. It follows his 2025 EP Catching Feelings with Italo disco legend Cerrone, and his 2024 album Hopecore, released under the name Rahim Redcar.

Chris will support the new double single with four full-band shows in Europe and the UK this December. He’ll perform in Brussels, London, and Amsterdam before closing out the run with a set at Alhambra in Paris. “We will revisit a repertoire that made us grow together, and give a first listen to unreleased songs from the next album,” Chris said in press materials. “We revisit, we reinterpret, we remember, and we transcend.”

entry.title: Saya Gray Drops Qwerty III EP
entry.summary: “I feel weird because we’re living in a weird world” — Jughead from Riverdale Saya Gray
entry.content:
With less than a week’s warning, Saya Gray has shared the third entry in her series of work-in-progress Qwerty EPs. The 7-track Qwerty III is the sequel to 2024’s Qwerty II and 2023’s Qwerty. You can stream it below.

“Q EPs are experiments between projects,” Gray elaborated in a statement accompanying the release. “The throwaways. The cathartic moments that don’t fit between eras of change.” She continued, “I feel weird because we’re living in a weird world, and these lil mixtapes are my documentation of that feeling.”

Last year saw Gray put out the LP Saya, which she claimed as her proper debut album (she’d previously released the full-length 19 Masters in 2022). This Monday, November 9, Gray will play the new songs from Qwerty III live at a free house show at 526 W 114th Street in New York.

entry.title: Kurt Vile Shreds Through “99 BPM” on Fallon
entry.summary: On the eve of the next leg of his North American tour
entry.content:
Still cruising through the promo circuit behind his June album Philadelphia’s Been Good to Me, Kurt Vile appeared on last night’s episode of The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon to perform “99 BPM.” Watch him stage a masterclass in the understated shred below.

Vile is gearing up for the latest North American leg of his tour behind the album. He returns to the road for a show in Buffalo, New York, tomorrow, to launch a run that proceeds to take in much of the American South.

Read Sam Sodomsky’s Q&A with the ageless songwriter around the LP, Kurt Vile Is Chasing Everything.

entry.title: Charlotte Adigéry and Bolis Pupul Line Up New Album and Tour
entry.summary: Watch the acrobatic “From Healer to Dealer” video from Topical Dancer follow-up Mainland Madinina
entry.content:
Electro-pop acrobats Charlotte Adigéry and Bolis Pupul are cartwheeling back into action with a new album, Mainland Madinina, and tour dates in North America and Europe. The Topical Dancer follow-up again features production from Soulwax, whose Deewee label is releasing the record alongside Because. After the Belgians returned in September with the parenthood-themed “Googoo Gaga,” new song “From Healer to Dealer” satirizes wellness culture through characters named Grace and Ruben. The video, a high-octane aerobic montage, is directed by Lennert Madou. Watch it below, and scroll down for the 2027 dates.

Adigéry said of Soulwax in a press release, “They’re people who can really inspire us when we get stuck—they invite us to go deeper, to really grasp the intention behind the song.” Pupul adds, “They’re still the musical chiropractors—they really know where to push when stuck.”

entry.title: Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross Are Back at It (Scoring David Fincher Movies)
entry.summary: The duo’s work on The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth will be their sixth collaboration
entry.content:
Like David Fincher was going to get someone else to score The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. Pitchfork can confirm the filmmaker has reunited with longtime collaborators Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross for his forthcoming Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood spinoff. It hits theaters November 25, with a Netflix premiere set for December 23. The film stars Brad Pitt, reprising his role as Booth, alongside Elizabeth Debicki, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, and Scott Caan.

The Nine Inch Nails duo have scored Fincher’s last six movies, dating back to 2010’s The Social Network, which netted them Oscars for Best Original Score. You can revisit some of their film work in our rundown of The 50 Best Movie Scores of All Time.
